llm.summary: Two things changed overnight and both are macro, not micro: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sending crude sharply higher, and the bond sell-off deepened with the 10-year at a 19-year high and mortgage rates back above 7%. That combination — higher oil plus higher yields plus a two-month-high dollar — is pure stagflationary impulse at the margin, and it broke gold (-3%) and silver (-5%) violently as Fed *hike* bets, not cut bets, get repriced. The offsetting good news is real: the US and China agreed to cut tariffs on roughly $60B of goods after the Trump-Xi summit, though the product lists leave rare earths and the hard issues unresolved. Nvidia dominated the tape with an historic $150B buyback addition (program upsized toward $235B) and the launch of an Open Agent Safety Platform with 100+ partners, explicitly pitched as what could have stopped the Hugging Face hack — that is Nvidia extending from silicon into the agent control plane, which is a bigger long-run moat story than the buyback. SpaceX put Starship into orbit for the first time. Sector rotation is still the narrowest tape in memory — Technology +66, Energy +27, and literally everything else between -21 and -94 — with growth beating value by 96 points, but energy's flow reading tripled from +8 to +27, which directly revives our ~21% EOG/COP/OXY sleeve that was dead money on Friday. The week is an event minefield: PCE, the jobs report, consumer confidence, 22 Fed events, and Micron earnings, which is the single largest binary in the book. Regime drift is unresolved in an informative way: Contraction +6.5 to 25.4 and Goldilocks +3.8 to 26.6 while Reflation collapses -7.4 — the market cannot decide whether 5% yields mean strong growth or an approaching break.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: risk is being taken in exactly two places and liquidated everywhere else. Nasdaq futures fell ~1% on the oil spike even as Nvidia set a record buyback — that is the tell that the constraint is the discount rate, not AI demand. With oil re-accelerating on the Hormuz stalemate and the long end making new highs, the headline-inflation channel that had briefly relaxed on Friday has re-tightened, and Fed hike pricing is now the dominant variable for every asset. Gold and silver are the clean casualties: $1.05 trillion of value gone as real yields and the dollar dominate, and that trade stays broken until the dollar rolls. Our energy sleeve is the immediate beneficiary — energy rotation +27 versus +8 Friday, Trump 'very seriously' weighing a diesel export ban, Morgan Stanley turning positive on oil names, Bessent saying Iran could have nothing left to trade in two weeks. Tactically: stay long AI infrastructure and energy, own nothing that needs the long end to fall, and expect a violent single-day reversal on any PCE or payroll surprise given how narrow the leadership base is.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the core conflict is an accelerating AI capex cycle financed into a rising cost of capital, with an oil shock now layered on top. Nvidia's $150B buyback is a statement that management sees cash flows as durable and the stock as cheap relative to them — but it is also a signal that at 5% risk-free rates, buying your own equity beats most alternative uses of cash, which is a subtly bearish message for the broader capex complex. Snowflake's $3.5B convertible getting punished for dilution and Datadog falling 19% on an 'AI customer cut' show the market is already sorting AI winners from AI-adjacent spenders. The tariff cuts on $60B of goods are a genuine disinflationary offset for Q1 goods CPI but are small relative to a $15-20 move in crude; net, the stagflation bucket stays live and Fitch's warning that an AI-driven correction could push the US into recession is the right tail to respect. Housing is where the damage compounds: 7%+ mortgages freeze turnover, push spend from moving to remodeling, and credit card delinquency at Great-Recession levels in NH is the leading edge of consumer stress that shows up in Q4 discretionary earnings. Expect concentration to intensify before it breaks: memory, power generation, oil, and agentic-AI control layers keep the bid; small caps, REITs, staples and utilities stay funding sources.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: a ~5% risk-free rate permanently re-rates owners of physical chokepoints — barrels, electrons, memory bits, refining capacity, fissile fuel — above narrative-priced asset-light stories. The Hormuz episode is a reminder that energy security is a geopolitical instrument, not a commodity trade, and that US shale and LNG operators are structurally short-listed buyers of global optionality; the fact that a single presidential sentence moved crude and the entire yield curve shows how thin the spare-capacity cushion is. Second, the agent control plane becomes an industry: Nvidia assembling 100+ partners around open agent safety after real rogue-agent incidents means governance, identity and containment become mandatory line items in every enterprise AI budget — that converts cybersecurity from a defensive cost center into a growth adjacency and further entrenches whoever owns the reference architecture. Third, power and compute merge into one asset class: ERCOT's 2030s demand surge from data centers, Duke guiding 2026 profit higher, Fermi contracting gas turbine O&M — generation gets pricing power it has not had in decades. Fourth, capital markets intermediation and hard assets both win from the debt regime, while businesses whose moat was cheap capital — marginal housing, levered consumer, non-cash-generative AI aspirants with 'big dreams and tiny revenue' IPOs — stay disadvantaged for a long time.

short_term: Households are being priced out of mobility: 7%+ mortgages plus a 19-year-high 10-year mean people stay put, renovate instead of move, and rent longer — housing turnover is the shock absorber taking the hit.

Consumers are trading down and levering up simultaneously — NH credit card delinquency at levels unseen since the Great Recession signals the bottom two income quintiles are funding the same basket with credit, not income.
Investors have abandoned gold as an inflation hedge in favor of the dollar and short Treasuries — the 'store of value' need is being satisfied by yield, not metal, as long as real rates rise.

Attention is migrating to agentic AI as a practical tool rather than a novelty: rising queries for 'ai agents vs agentic ai', 'ai agent builder', 'ai agent vs chatbot' show users trying to operationalize, which is exactly why safety/containment became a product.

Retail curiosity is rotating toward stablecoins and cloud careers ('cloud computing salary/jobs/certification') — people are seeking income security via skill acquisition and monetary security via dollar-linked digital instruments.
Enterprises are re-pricing energy and logistics costs into planning after the oil spike, and a possible diesel export ban would hit freight, agriculture and construction cost structures within weeks.
long_term: Energy security becomes a consumer-visible category again — people will pay for reliability and price stability (fixed-rate utility plans, onsite generation, EV/hybrid mobility choices) the way they once paid only for convenience.

Trust and containment become purchasable goods in AI: as agents act autonomously, individuals and firms will demand audit trails, kill switches and identity — a durable spend category that did not exist three years ago.

Housing demand converts from ownership to optionality — build-to-rent, longer tenancy, multi-generational households — and the political backlash against private equity in housing (already in midterm campaigns) shapes the regulatory regime for a decade.

The 'status' good shifts from home equity to portfolio equity: when the S&P visibly outruns the housing market, younger cohorts allocate to markets instead of down payments, which structurally grows brokerage, fractional and self-directed platforms.

Compute and electricity become a joint household and corporate budget line, driving sustained demand for generation, grid and cooling, and normalizing data-center siting as a local political issue ('ai data center near me', water usage queries).
Knowledge work reorganizes around agent supervision rather than task execution — the scarce human skill becomes specifying, verifying and governing machine output.

At 8% this is correctly sized — do not add into a record-buyback announcement on a day the tape fell 1% on oil, since buybacks at highs historically coincide with cash-flow peaks.

The setup is favorable — chip-fab attention +47%, semicap flows improving, AI memory tight — but you are carrying full size into an event where HBM pricing commentary can re-rate the stock 15% either way. Decide consciously whether you want that exposure or want to trim to 5-6% ahead of the print.
